#158242. Tech Report: Survey Identifies Data Governance Enforcement Gap for Agentic AI Tools

📅 07 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (805 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Survey Identifies Data Governance Enforcement Gap for Agentic AI Tools

📅 07 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that according to a fresh survey from identity security firm Delinea, 99.7% of IT and security leaders noted their organization has a formal policy governing what data AI tools and agents are permitted to access.
  • That disconnect is at the center of Delinea's fall 2026 Identity Security Report, "The AI Enforcement Gap," which suggests companies have made quick progress establishing AI governance but have not necessarily built the technical controls needed to enforce it.
  • The findings come from a pair of surveys covering 2,254 IT and security leaders and 2,250 non-IT employees at organizations with at least 500 employees across the U.S, U.K, Germany, Australia, Singapore, UAE, France, and India.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that according to a fresh survey from identity security firm Delinea, 99.7% of IT and security leaders noted their organization has a formal policy governing what data AI tools and agents are permitted to access. Yet only about 51% said AI access is checked against those policies in real time. Perhaps more worrying is that only 19% said their organization could detect in real time when an agent last accessed data outside its intended scope.

That disconnect is at the center of Delinea's fall 2026 Identity Security Report, "The AI Enforcement Gap," which suggests companies have made quick progress establishing AI governance but have not necessarily built the technical controls needed to enforce it.

The findings come from a pair of surveys covering 2,254 IT and security leaders and 2,250 non-IT employees at organizations with at least 500 employees across the U.S, U.K, Germany, Australia, Singapore, UAE, France, and India.

All the organizations were using or piloting AI, while the employees surveyed used at least one AI tool for work.

The problem becomes more consequential as companies move from AI tools that primarily respond to users toward agents capable of taking actions on their behalf.

Eighty-seven percent of IT and security respondents stated their organization had experienced or suspected of an incident during the past year in which an AI tool or agent accessed sensitive information beyond what was required for its task.

Delinea's research also suggests companies are giving agents access that can persist longer than necessary. Only 58% of IT and security leaders said they have mechanisms that automatically revoke or expire AI access when a session ends, and those controls do not necessarily cover every agent or tool. Forty-two percent said many agent credentials remain active until an audit.

Agents also are not always receiving their own narrowly defined permissions. Half of IT leaders mentioned their organizations use the employee's existing permissions as a boundary for what an agent can access. That can effectively hand an agent years of accumulated access belonging to the person who debuted it.

That is particularly significant because an AI agent does not necessarily behave like a traditional service account. A service account typically performs a predefined process, while an agent can choose different tools, actions and sequences at runtime depending on the situation.

In a recent development, "Service accounts run fixed scripts," noted Mike Albrecht, associate director in the Risk Advisory Practice at Cross Country Consulting. "An AI agent decides what actions it's going to take at runtime.".

The enforcement problem is not limited to autonomous agents.

It has been revealed that the researchers found that 76% of employees surveyed had bypassed formal approval at some point to use AI tools with tech giant data, applications or systems. And 48% said they always or extensively use AI tools without going through formal approval.

Meanwhile, 60% stated they had felt pressure to use AI with sensitive or confidential information even when they were not sure doing so was permitted.

Executives were particularly likely to circumvent the process. Eighty-one percent of C-level respondents noted they always or regularly bypass AI access approval, compared with 33% of intermediate-level employees.

The result is a widening gap between written AI governance and what companies can see and control. Delinea found that only 41% of IT leaders noted all AI tools and agents accessing company data are actively monitored. When an AI tool or agent went outside its intended scope, 55% said it took at least a day to detect the incident, while 30% said detection took four days or longer.

That suggests the next phase of enterprise AI governance may depend less on writing additional rules and more on whether organizations can enforce existing ones while an agent is working.

Recent findings suggest that "Most organizations cannot confidently answer three questions: What agents are running in our environment? What can they access? What have they actually done?" said Delinea CEO Art Gilliland. "An agent can begin a session with legitimate access and drift into something it was never meant to do.".

The full report is available for download here.

    Latest Update: Claude Intros Sonnet 5.5 with Model-Switching Cybersecurity Safeguards

    📅 08 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's new Claude release, Sonnet 5.5, brings cybersecurity safeguards that can change which model handles a request during a Claude conversation.
    • According to Anthropic's explanation of model switching, automatic fallback is enabled by default in Claude.
    • It has been revealed that the company identifies penetration testing and exploit generation among activities that may trigger cybersecurity fallbacks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's new Claude release, Sonnet 5.5, brings cybersecurity safeguards that can change which model handles a request during a Claude conversation. Higher-risk tasks can fall back to Sonnet 5.

    According to Anthropic's explanation of model switching, automatic fallback is enabled by default in Claude. Consumers receive a notice, and the answer is labeled with the model that provided it. The chat then stays on Sonnet 5 unless the user changes the selection.

    It has been revealed that the company identifies penetration testing and exploit generation among activities that may trigger cybersecurity fallbacks. Source-code vulnerability scanning remains supported. Biology and reasoning-extraction safeguards can block requests outright, rather than route them elsewhere.

    It has been revealed that the distinction matters operationally. A block stops the request; a fallback allows an attempt to continue with a different model. Neither outcome should be treated as interchangeable with completion by the model the user originally chose.

    Anthropic indicates Sonnet 5.5 generates output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and can reduce cost per task by up to 30%, based on its testing. Token prices remain unchanged.

    It has been revealed that those claims describe performance under the company's test conditions. An organization evaluating the service also needs to examine what happens when its own assignments encounter safeguards.

    In a recent development, an internal pilot could record how often work is interrupted, whether fallback answers are usable, and when people need help. Such measurements would give buyers a more relevant basis for deployment than assuming every task receives the advertised model's capabilities.

    Anthropic has declared prepares to expand its Cyber Verification Program with tiered access for Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, and Mythos models. Its current program guidance explicitly excludes the two new 5.5 models and states the expansion is forthcoming.

    Organizations should distinguish those planned arrangements from access available today.

    It has been revealed that the broader enterprise issue is accountability. When an AI service changes models during an assignment, someone still needs to determine whether the resulting work is suitable. A visible handoff helps, but organizations must decide how employees should respond to it.

    For more information on Sonnet 5.5, go to the Anthropic site.

    A track record of published, data heavy research that institutions or serious media rely on.

    Deep understanding of market structure: exchanges, spot and derivatives, liquidity, onchain flows and proof of reserves.

    Strong quantitative skills and hands on data work (SQL or Python, APIs, large datasets).

    Excellent written English and the judgement to present sensitive findings neutrally and accurately.

    Experience leading or mentoring analysts.

    Background at a crypto data provider, an institutional research desk or a TradFi data business.

    Understanding of how data is packaged and sold to institutions (licensing, enterprise feeds, research subscriptions).

    Knowledge of tokenized assets, RWAs or traditional market data.

    Existing relationships with tier one financial and crypto media.

    Comfort using AI tools to automate data pulls and drafts.

    Mandarin, given our close work with Chinese speaking partners and media.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that recent research from Thales highlights how AI adoption and emerging quantum computing threats are putting pressure on existing security measures. The 2026 Thales Data Threat Report: Quantum & AI Trends, based on responses from 3,120 security and IT management professionals across 20 countries, found that 98% are considering how the two technologies affect each other. Thirty percent reported a significant increase in security budgets specifically for AI.

    Sources indicate that the research, conducted by 451 Research by S&P Global, examines both the risks and potential benefits of the technologies. Fifty-seven percent believe quantum computing will enhance machine learning, while 54% expect it to enable advanced simulations of complex systems. The security findings span data governance, cloud infrastructure, and preparations for quantum-resistant encryption.

    Cloud-based storage, cloud-delivered applications, and cloud management infrastructure were the three most frequently cited asset types targeted by attackers, at 35%, 34%, and 32%, respectively. The report connects that exposure to the large datasets required for AI training and the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

    According to recent reports, organizations are also looking to cloud providers for protection: 67% reported investing in their cloud provider's AI-specific security tools, compared with 63% using an established security provider. Respondents could identify multiple sources of protection, including startups, large language model providers, and internally developed controls.

    In a recent development, encryption coverage remains incomplete. Only 7% of organizations reported encrypting more than 80% of their sensitive cloud data, while 29% reported encrypting more than 60%. The report's chart puts the average share encrypted at 47% in 2026, down from 51% in 2025.

    The findings extend concerns raised in coverage of Thales' 2025 cloud security research, when AI security already ranked second to cloud security in spending priorities and 52% of respondents reported that AI security spending was displacing existing security budgets. The latest report again places AI security second, while its historical comparison reveals average sensitive cloud data encryption coverage falling from 51% in 2025 to 47% in 2026.

    AI security was the second-highest prioritized security spending category overall, behind cloud security. But protecting data ranked much lower among the measures organizations use to judge AI projects: Reducing or managing risks of data loss or noncompliance placed sixth among seven success criteria, at 35%.

    Improving customer experience led those measures at 68%, followed by reducing employee toil through greater task automation at 63%. Meanwhile, poor data quality or initial data governance was the leading inhibitor to AI adoption, cited by 65%; security risks from exposed data followed at 61%. Another 51% cited AI initiatives moving too quickly to be properly secured.

    Technology directors touch nearly everything that happens in a school system. Here are three strategies these IT leaders can use to navigate their many duties without losing strategic focus, influence, or sustainability.

    Carahsoft has created a new community for K-12 schools and districts designed to help education leaders navigate AI adoption and cyber readiness.

    OpenAI has declared it will retire Custom GPTs and move the specialized workflows built around them to a new plugin architecture spanning ChatGPT and its Codex coding agent.

    SMART Technologies has introduced SoundFlow, a plug-and-play broadcasting system that allows classroom audio content to flow directly from a SMART Board display to students' compatible hearing aids, earbuds, headphones, personal listening devices, or speakers.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Most growth teams call themselves data-driven. They have a dashboard, an agency and a ChatGPT licence to write ad copy faster. That’s the 99%.

    We want to be part of the 0.1%: a tech giant where AI doesn’t just help the growth team, it runs the growth loop. Every day, on every channel.

    Then it’s your chance to define a newly introduced category : The Operating System (OS) for Human Greatness Augmented with AI.

    Science-backed. Design-led. AI-powered. Global.

    Recent findings suggest that we’re not looking for someone who only advises on what to test, we’re looking for someone who builds it. A hands-on Head of Growth who can ideate, write the copy, design the strategy and launch experiments directly.

    Our growth machine has to be able to:.

    1. Generate hypotheses. Read the signals (ad performance, webinar attendance, sales calls, objections, churn reasons, comments, competitors’ ads) and propose what to test next, with a cost and an expected impact.

    According to recent reports, 2. Act across every tool. Not a chatbot in a tab: it reads and writes in our whole stack, from ad accounts to CRM, landing pages, webinars, email, social DMs and analytics.

    3. Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, offers, voice, member stories, past campaigns and what they taught us, in one shared company brain.

    4. Ship its hypotheses. Produce the hook, the ad cut, the page, the email sequence or the funnel variant, and put it live.

    Sources indicate that 5. Measure with real KPIs. Every test is tied to a number that matters (cost per qualified lead, show-up rate, close rate, CAC, payback, LTV), not to likes or reach.

    Sources indicate that 6. Learn and loop on its own. Scale what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and launch the next cycle without waiting for a meeting.

    In a recent development, this is already real. Our growth hub tracks every hypothesis and experiment, with its result. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content, prepare webinars, wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations and audit our tracking after every live. Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day.

    We believe self-help is broken: generic theory, a quick high, no real change.

    We believe people deserve more. More than content. More than motivation.

    They deserve a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

    Growth at Paradox means bringing people into something that actually changes their life, and proving it.

    - Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors).

    - Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals).

    - Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys).

    To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

    Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world.

    According to recent reports, here’s the bet: a organization that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. A small growth team running a self-learning machine can out-test, out-learn and out-grow teams a hundred times its size.

    In a recent development, we hold ourselves to the standards of Apple, Spotify and MasterClass. While others hide their numbers, we let our results speak.

    As Head of Growth, you’ll be the architect of a growth machine that learns by itself. In a classic growth team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the work, you design the system, set the bar and make the calls.

    You don’t just manage a team, you get your hands dirty to identify growth levers and pull them yourself.

    ❌ The old way: a Head of Growth hires people and agencies, briefs them, and checks their work.

    According to recent reports, 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: your team is mostly agents, and you build them yourself. You write their skills, plug them into our tools (ad accounts, CRM, webinars, email, analytics) and write the evals that tell an agent what "good" means: a hook that stops the scroll, a page that converts, a test that’s worth its cost.

    You give autonomy step by step: first an agent suggests, then it acts once you approve, then it acts alone within a budget and guardrails. You move each agent up a level only when its track record earns it.

    According to recent reports, example: in your first month you build the agent that reviews every ad set overnight. At first it only suggests. By month three it pauses losers and moves budget by itself within limits you set, and you only see what was decided and why.

    ❌ The old way: a media buyer checks the dashboards each morning, changes bids by hand and waits for the weekly report.

    🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build and improve the agents that watch every ad set, page, webinar and email sequence around the clock. They spot what’s dropping, find the cause, fix it or launch a variant, and report what they did.

    In a recent development, you give autonomy step by step: an agent can pause an ad on its own long before it can raise a budget. You decide where each agent stops and a human takes over.

    Example: show-up rate drops on Tuesday’s webinar. Before anyone notices, an agent has found the cause (a reminder that never went out), fixed it and started testing a fresh reminder sequence.

    ❌ The old way: a creative team briefs an agency, waits two weeks and gets five ads.

    🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build the agents that turn every live, interview and member story into hooks, ad cuts and shorts, that study what the best advertisers in the world are running, and that write in our voice.

    Your taste becomes the eval: you write down what makes a great hook, a great cut and a great story, in rules and examples the agents check themselves against. Each time you reject something, the reason goes back into the rules.

    Example: one webinar becomes dozens of hook variants by the next morning. You keep the best few, and next week the agents’ first drafts are already closer to your bar.

    ❌ The old way: an analyst rebuilds the numbers in a spreadsheet at the end of the month, and nobody trusts them.

    🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build the agents that connect every touch to cash, from ad to lead, live, sale and transformed member, and that audit the tracking after every campaign.

    No number, no test: you define the KPIs that matter (CAC, show-up, close rate, LTV, payback), and agents refuse to launch a test that isn’t wired to one.

    Example: after each live, an agent cross-checks the ad platform, the CRM and our analytics, finds where they disagree and fixes the leak before the next live.

    ❌ The old way: lessons live in people’s heads and leave with them.

    🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: every result goes back into the company brain, and agents read it before proposing anything. The machine never learns the same lesson twice.

    You measure the machine itself: tests per week, time from idea to live, the share of the work done without a human, and how many agents moved up an autonomy level this month. You push those numbers up.

    According to recent reports, and always: no fake scarcity, no fake claims, real stories told with consent. The machine can scale, but it doesn’t decide what’s right. You do.

    It has been revealed that how you’ll know you’re AI-native: you spend your time building agents, writing evals and making calls, not doing the work by hand. Most experiments are generated and shipped by agents. The output grows every month while the headcount doesn’t.

    You’ll own these KPIs: LTV / CAC ratio, funnel conversion rate by stage, experiments launched per week.

    Desired outcomes: conversion rates 2x better than baseline, growth experimentation that runs continuously, a predictable growth engine.

    You have ideally a minimum of 3 years of experience in Conversion Rate Optimization, Growth Experimentation, or Performance Marketing, ideally within SaaS, e-commerce, or digital product environments.

    You have a track record of designing, implementing, and scaling A/B and multivariate tests that have generated measurable improvements in revenue, user activation, or conversion.

    You’ve built with AI and agents yourself: Claude Code, automations, APIs, evals, creative pipelines. Show us something you built, not a certificate.

    A Conversion Architect, skilled at diagnosing funnel bottlenecks and translating data into structured experimentation roadmaps that deliver measurable business outcomes.

    A Behavioral Strategist, fascinated by what drives human action, able to mix cognitive psychology, UX, and persuasion frameworks to design experiences that convert because they resonate.

    A Data-driven Creator, fluent in GA4, Hotjar, AB Tasty, VWO, Amplitude, not just running tests, but connecting insights to revenue, retention, and lifetime value.

    Loop thinker: you see every channel as a loop that can learn, and you can’t stop yourself from closing it.

    Taste: you know a great hook in two seconds, and you’d rather ship one great ad than ten average ones.

    Sources indicate that numbers-honest: you say when a test failed. You care about real revenue, not vanity metrics.

    Builder, not manager: you’d rather build the system than coordinate an agency.

    Growth over ego: you love hard feedback, you read, study and learn fast.

    Cross-disciplinary: you move from psychology to spreadsheet to creative brief to code.

    Analytical: you turn a vague problem into a clear hypothesis, a metric and an experiment.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    -> 📚 150€ of books or education - At Paradox, we are learner lovers and we want to support you in that.

    Industry observers note that ⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this : do not apply ⚠️.

    If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀🚀🚀.

    That job description resonated with you?

    Here is your tailor made hiring process.

    📃 A 6 to 8 minutes application survey (with a short video assignment).

    Our recruitment process is tailored to do our best to avoid that you or us realize that we’re not a perfect fit. Every step serves a purpose and will allow us to get to know you better as much as it’ll help you understand more where you’ll be stepping in.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We are hiring 2026 and 2027 Graduate Software Engineers into engineering teams around the world.
    • If you are excited about the potential that open source has for humanity and the enterprise, you have outstanding results in your academic career, and you are excited to contribute to the open source stack, this is the best way to apply to Canonical.
    • Most of our engineering teams work from home.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We are hiring 2026 and 2027 Graduate Software Engineers into engineering teams around the world. As a global platform manufacturer we offer a wide range of software engineering challenges, in both open source products and commercial business systems. We have teams that work in a variety of languages, typically Python, Golang, Rust, C/C++, JavaScript and of course... Bash. We work from the very lowest levels of the Linux system - BIOS and boot loaders, firmware, kernel and drivers, all the way up to desktop applications and containers. We work on tiny devices like the Raspberry Pi and fresh RISC-V boards, all the way up to supercomputers, clouds and Kubernetes clusters. We work on compilers and toolchains, and we work on security, cryptography, performance and documentation. Some of our teams focus on packaging thousands of pieces of software, others focus on deep contributions to a single body of code.

    If you are excited about the potential that open source has for humanity and the enterprise, you have outstanding results in your academic career, and you are excited to contribute to the open source stack, this is the best way to apply to Canonical. We will work with you to identify teams and projects that would be interesting and a good fit for your skills and motivations. The process is highly competitive, it will require effort and excellence to succeed if you apply here.

    Most of our engineering teams work from home. We try to align a single team in a single time zone - EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia Pacific and Indian Ocean), and AMER (North, South and Central Americas). Even though you work from home, we try to ensure you always have colleagues alongside to coach and mentor you, and for the companionship of shared problem solving and pair programming. Larger projects have multiple teams and might span the globe. We work with the open source community and specialize in building teams that work well in the 'fishbowl' of open source engineering. This is full time work, five days a week, often solving hard problems with significant responsibility. We don't generally work weekends and nights and we do enjoy good holidays but we also expect productive and intense engagement Monday to Friday.

    We bring all our engineering teams together in person twice a year for a deep 'sprint' with other teams to stimulate discussion and enable a wide range of career development paths. This is a fantastic way to demonstrate and develop your skill in software, learn about a wide range of technologies, make a meaningful impact to open source, and see some very interesting new cities that you might never otherwise get to visit.

    If you find the open source stack amazing, and you have been a consistent high-performing student in your school and university, then this will be a challenging and exciting start to your career.

    Location: This is a Globally remote role.

    We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We assess performance and revisit compensation twice annually to ensure we recognize outstanding colleagues. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

    Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. We are founder-led, profitable, and growing.

    It has been revealed that powered by worldwide distributed collaboration since our inception in 2004, we believe tech and business leadership can emerge anywhere. We have no central headquarters. Most of us work from home, but we are exceptionally disciplined about this. We have very high expectations of all colleagues, and are champions of excellence. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

    It has been revealed that we are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

    Flashpoint Receives Patent for Ransomware Risk Model, Tying Vulnerabilites to Likelihood of Attack

    📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, cybersecurity tech giant Flashpoint announced it has received U.S.
    • The patent comes at a time when security teams are confronting a growing vulnerability problem: Flashpoint's Global Threat Intelligence Report: 2026 Midyear Edition tracked 21,667 vulnerability disclosures during the first half of 2026, an 8% increase.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, cybersecurity tech giant Flashpoint announced it has received U.S. Patent No. 12,705,360 for its Ransomware Risk model, a methodology designed to help security teams determine which newly disclosed vulnerabilities more closely resemble those historically used in ransomware attacks.

    The patent comes at a time when security teams are confronting a growing vulnerability problem: Flashpoint's Global Threat Intelligence Report: 2026 Midyear Edition tracked 21,667 vulnerability disclosures during the first half of 2026, an 8% increase.

    Of those, 4,015, or around 19 percent, already had public or functional exploit code. Flashpoint also reported a 45 percent increase in Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) attacks during the period.

    Sources indicate that the patent was granted August 11 2026, although the underlying Ransomware Risk model isn't fresh. It has been available through Flashpoint Vulnerability Intelligence since 2022.

    The model addresses a basic vulnerability-management problem: severity and real-world ransomware risk aren't necessarily the same thing, because severity scores do not necessarily indicate which flaws attackers are most likely to target.

    Recent findings suggest that the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, or CVSS, measures how severe a vulnerability could be. The Exploit Prediction Scoring System, or EPSS, estimates the probability of exploitation more broadly.

    Flashpoint's Ransomware Risk model adds another dimension by comparing newly disclosed vulnerabilities with the characteristics of flaws previously exploited in ransomware attacks.

    Industry observers note that that could change where a vulnerability lands in an organization's patching queue. A lower-severity flaw might normally sit behind numerous critical vulnerabilities. But if its characteristics closely resemble vulnerabilities repeatedly targeted by ransomware operators, security teams may have reason to move it higher.

    "A severity score alone can't tell you which vulnerabilities pose the greatest real-world risk of exploitation by ransomware actors," Flashpoint CEO Josh Lefkowitz stated. "Our patented Ransomware Risk model applies years of threat intelligence to that problem, giving customers an earlier signal and helping them prioritize based on how attackers actually operate.".

    The firm's midyear research also illustrates the scale of the prioritization problem. Its vulnerability intelligence covers traditional IT systems as well as cloud, IoT, operational technology, open source software. and third-party libraries.

    The tech giant indicates it also tracks more than 105,000 vulnerabilities that aren't represented in CVE or the National Vulnerability Database, expanding the pool of flaws that security teams may need to evaluate.

    The cybersecurity organization's patented methodology profiles vulnerabilities using more than 60 technical characteristics, including whether a flaw can be exploited remotely without authentication, whether it affects operational technology systems, and how exploitation could affect data availability.

    In a recent development, those characteristics form a multi-factor fingerprint. The model maps each vulnerability against clusters containing flaws previously exploited in ransomware attacks and assigns a Low, Medium, High, or Critical Ransomware Risk rating.

    Flashpoint claims the rating can be generated when a vulnerability is disclosed, rather than requiring security teams to wait for public evidence of active exploitation. Ratings are then updated as new ransomware activity and threat intelligence emerge.

    Within Flashpoint Ignite, Ransomware Risk appears alongside CVSS, EPSS, Social Risk, and exploit maturity. The idea isn't to replace existing scoring systems, but to give administrators additional information when deciding what to remediate first.

    Nor does a High or Critical Ransomware Risk rating mean a vulnerability will necessarily be exploited. The model measures how closely its characteristics resemble vulnerabilities historically associated with ransomware attacks.

    In a recent development, for security teams facing thousands of potential vulnerabilities, that distinction matters. The flaw carrying the highest severity score isn't necessarily the one that most closely resembles what ransomware operators have historically chosen to attack.

    "Despite being the most popular indicator for priority, we know that severity alone doesn't tell you whether a vulnerability will be exploited or used in ransomware," said Ben Haynes, Data Science & Analytics Lead at Flashpoint and co-inventor of the patented methodology.

    "A vulnerability can score low on a traditional severity scale and still share the characteristics we repeatedly see in ransomware attacks.".

    For more information, go to the Flashpoint site.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What if your next playground was to build a global, iconic Brand, with a creative machine that never sleeps, and compounds?

    Sources indicate that we’re not looking for a "Social Media Manager" to follow a calendar. We’re looking for an AI-native Creative Director (Brand & Content).

    Someone who understands that to win today, you don’t just need "content", you need a Movement.

    According to recent reports, this isn’t another content job. Most content teams use AI to write captions faster. That’s the 99%. We want to be in the 0.1%: a media where AI runs the creative loop, from the signal to the hook, the cut, the post and the lesson. Every day, on every platform, in French and in English. You bring the taste. The machine you build brings the scale.

    Here’s the bet: a manufacturer that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. We aim for $10M in revenue with 10 people, each of them running a dozen agents.

    Paradoxically, the more AI runs our content, the more human it has to feel. AI doesn’t make more of what everyone makes. It makes more of what only we can make.

    Our creative machine has to be able to:.

    1. Read the signals. Comments, DMs, retention graphs, saves, shares, search trends, objections from sales calls, and what the best creators and advertisers in the world are publishing right now.

    It has been revealed that 2. Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, years of interviews, lives and courses, member stories, and every past post with what it taught us, in one shared firm brain.

    3. Generate in our voice. Hooks, scripts, shorts, carousels, cuts, thumbnails and captions, in French and in English.

    According to recent reports, 4. Ship. Format, schedule, publish and answer, on every platform.

    In a recent development, 5. Measure with real KPIs. Retention, shares, saves, follower growth, and the followers who become leads and members. Not likes.

    According to recent reports, 6. Learn and loop on its own. Double down on what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and start the next cycle without waiting for a meeting.

    It has been revealed that this is already real. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content and wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations. And our product is AI-native too: Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day.

    At Paradox, we are convinced that greatness is trainable, and we believe self-help is broken.

    Most learning platforms are used the same way: consuming generic theories, getting quick highs, ending with no real change.

    People deserve more: a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

    That’s why we want to empower people at scale, by leveraging cutting edge technologies like AI, and crafting user experiences with outstanding aesthetics.

    - Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors).

    - Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals).

    - Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys).

    To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

    Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world.

    You lead the Content Factory not by management, but with creativity.

    In a classic content team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the volume, you design the machine, set the bar and make the calls. Humans do what no machine can: taste.

    Build a symbiotic strategy where David Laroche’s personal brand and Paradox’s firm brand reinforce each other without cannibalization.

    Implement radical upcoming formats (documentaries, conceptual shorts) that shatter the boring codes of the "Self-Help" industry.

    Define distinct, sharp editorial lines for each platform: Depth & Search for YouTube, Aesthetic & Vibe for Instagram, and Authority & Authenticity for LinkedIn.

    ❌ The old way: a strategy deck written once a year, and a calendar filled by habit.

    🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents watch every platform, every competitor and every comment continuously. They tell you which angle is rising, which format is tiring and which story our audience asks for. The strategy updates every week, on evidence.

    Take responsibility for the entire production chain from hooks to storyboarding the narrative, and ensuring the final cut matches the vision.

    Own the packaging: titles, thumbnails and the first 3 seconds. You test variants every week and know your click-through and retention numbers by heart.

    ❌ The old way: one shoot becomes one video and a handful of posts.

    According to recent reports, 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: one shoot, one live or one interview becomes dozens of hooks, shorts, carousels and ad cuts by the next morning, in both languages. Concepts are tested with AI-generated drafts before we spend a day shooting them.

    It has been revealed that your taste becomes the eval. You write down what makes a great hook, a great cut, a great carousel and a great story, in rules and examples the agents check themselves against. Each time you reject something, the reason goes back into the rules.

    Act as the final quality check: nothing gets published if it doesn’t meet the "Paradox Standard" of aesthetics and storytelling, whether a person or an agent made it.

    ❌ The old way: a creative team briefs an editor, waits three days and gets two versions.

    In a recent development, 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents draft, cut, caption, translate and schedule. You keep the best, and next week their first drafts are already closer to your bar.

    Analyze retention graphs, CTR, and CPL to iterate based on feedback, killing what fails and aggressively scaling what works.

    ❌ The old way: someone pulls the stats at the end of the month and nobody changes anything.

    Sources indicate that 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: agents read the numbers of every post every day, explain why it worked or didn’t, and propose the next test. You measure the machine itself: posts per week, time from idea to live, hit rate, and the share of the work done without a human.

    We started in French. You build the machine that takes Paradox to English-speaking audiences: channels, formats and voice that feel native, not translated.

    And always: real stories told with consent, no fake claims, no fake scarcity. The machine can scale, but it doesn’t decide what’s right. You do.

    In a recent development, how you’ll know you’re AI-native: you spend your time on concepts, taste and calls, not on resizing, captioning and exporting. The output grows every month while the team doesn’t.

    Proven Content Builder: You have successfully grown a media brand, a YouTube channel, or a personal brand to significant scale (100k+ followers or millions of views). You understand the mechanics of virality and retention. You’ve created at least one format that broke out, and you can show its click-through and retention numbers.

    Elite Scripting Skills: You can show us scripts you wrote that performed. You know how to structure a narrative, write a hook that stops the scroll, and keep an audience engaged for 20+ minutes.

    Performance Fluency: You have worked in environments where content had to drive business results (ads, rolls out, conversion), not just vanity metrics.

    AI-native Creative: you’ve built content pipelines with AI yourself: Claude Code, automations, generative video, image and voice tools, evals. Show us something you built, not a certificate.

    Industry observers note that intolerant to Mediocrity: You have "Taste." You are physically pained by a bad font, a clumsy cut, or a weak headline. You fight for the details that others ignore, including in what AI produces.

    Psychology Obsessed: You don’t just "make content"; you study human nature. You constantly ask why people click, why they share, and what emotion drives them.

    A "Doer" with Authority: You command respect not by title, but by competence. You can jump into a project, write the script, direct the shoot, and fix the edit if needed.

    Loop thinker: you see every platform as a loop that can learn, and you can’t stop yourself from closing it.

    It has been revealed that no Ego, Just Impact: You don’t fall in love with your ideas. You accept that even the best concepts can flop. When it happens, you don’t take it personally; you analyze the data, pivot immediately, and ship the next concept with renewed energy.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    Our chosen language for written communication is English.

    ❌ If you need clarity before chaos: wrong place.

    ❌ If you prefer balance over intensity: wrong season.

    ❌ If you don’t genuinely care about the topics we cover: wrong place.

    ❌ If you want to strategize without getting your hands dirty in scripting, directing, or the editing suite: wrong role.

    ❌ If you think AI content means generic content: wrong role. We use AI to multiply what only we can make.

    ❌ If you want to manage a large team: we’d rather build the machine than grow the headcount.

    Help us market a product that fuses neuroscience, design, and AI to reinvent how humans grow.

    Build one of the first truly AI-native media, and write the playbook others will copy.

    Work with filmmakers, psychologists, engineers, and creatives obsessed with impact.

    You’ll compete with San Francisco companies.

    -> 🏅 Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform.

    But you don’t just want a competitive paycheck, you also want….

    -> Playing a crucial role in the development of a firm whose content and products will be used by millions of people.

    -> Waking up in the morning feeling like you are making a difference is something!

    We receive messages every day from clients who have successfully lost weight, quit smoking, reached a milestone in their business, built better relationships, and made positive changes in their lives.

    But that’s not all, we believe that driven people deserve….

    -> 😎 A organization culture based on autonomy & accountability.

    -> 🗽 Flexible working hours (but very hard working).

    -> 🌎 A remote culture from day one with the freedom to work from wherever you want.

    -> 🧍‍♀️ Standing desks paid by the tech giant if you live far from our offices.

    -> 💻 Work on Mac, for us it counts :).

    -> 🏀 350€ per year paid by the company to take care of yourself (for your gym, or dance class or whatever make you feel great).

    -> 📚 150€ of books or education - At Paradox, we are learner lovers and we want to support you in that.

    -> 🔥 Access to Athena - our Paradox AI Coach supporting you on anything personal or professional, we want you to live your best life.

    In a recent development, ⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this : do not apply ⚠️.

    If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀🚀🚀.

    That job description resonated with you?

    Here is your tailor made hiring process.

    📃 A 6 to 8 minutes application survey, with links to content you made and something you built with AI.

    💻 A 30mn video call with Timy, HR, to deep dive into your career path and ambitions.

    💻 A 1h video call, to discuss how you’d fit into Paradox’s content team.

    💻 A 1h culture-fit video call, to assess alignment with our values and mindset.

    💻 A 1h final video call with David, CEO, to discuss the creative vision and the next milestones to build.

    💼 Reference check to understand how you operate across environments and help set you up for a smooth onboarding.

    Our recruitment process is tailored to do our best to avoid that you or us realize that we’re not a perfect fit. Every step serves a purpose and will allow us to get to know you better as much as it’ll help you understand more where you’ll be stepping in.

    We also want you to have time to ask all of your questions regarding the mission, the long-term vision of your team and the company, our values, with the relevant interlocutor in front of you.

    If you’re not joining to post content.

    If you’re here to build a media that changes how millions of people grow.

    Let’s build the Operating System for Greatness.

    It has been revealed that we’re looking for a senior product designer to be the first dedicated designer on our product growth team, shaping how creators get set up, see value in their first days, and enjoy a seamless upgrade experience. Kit ships fast, and the product growth team builds the frameworks and systems that connect creators to the value in their plan as the product keeps changing. We need a designer who can balance rapid experimentation with long-term value for our creators.

    Sources indicate that product growth is a newly introduced team at Kit, formed earlier this year. In the six months since, we’ve found our rhythm and started to move the numbers, but we’re still shaping how we work, how we prioritise and where we focus in the long term. As the team’s designer, you’ll be the design voice for growth, with real influence over how the team works and what it builds.

    According to recent reports, you'll own the design of the moments that move our funnel: onboarding, activation, free trials, upgrade and upsell flows, pricing and checkout, and billing. You'll work in a team that learns by shipping, through A/B tests and ship-and-measure changes, and you'll use data to decide what to try next.

    This is a full-time IC role for a designer who loves connecting design decisions to numbers, moves rapidly without sacrificing quality, and is excited about using AI to accelerate outcomes.

    We need someone who thinks deeply about user behaviour, interaction design and the product experience, and who is proactive about finding the next opportunity rather than waiting for a spec.

    Sources indicate that you'll report to Dan Winer, Director of Product Design, and join a small, high-impact product design team presently consisting of four senior product designers and a senior design engineer. From day one, you’ll be part of the product growth team’s product trio alongside the product manager and engineering manager, shaping the team’s vision, priorities and how we work. You’ll also work closely with the team’s engineers.

    First week: Get to know Kit’s product and the product growth team’s goals. Get access to Figma, Linear, Mixpanel and our other reporting tools. Take part in get-to-know-you calls with the team.

    Industry observers note that first month: Get up to speed on how we track and measure creator behaviour in Mixpanel, Omni and Clarity, which experiments are running now, and what we’ve learnt from past ones. Join the product trio’s planning and prioritisation discussions, and ship a small experiment or two, with support from the Director of Product Design as you take ownership of the growth work.

    In a recent development, first six months: Own design across the team’s work, which spans growth (onboarding, activation, trials and upgrades) and billing (checkout, plan changes, downgrades and cancellation). This might include personalising onboarding, improving free-to-paid conversion or simplifying our payment flows. By six months, the team should rely on you for a clear picture of how creators move through these flows, where they get stuck and why. You’ll help the team run more and better experiments, from forming a hypothesis to reading the results. We don’t have dedicated researchers, so you’ll talk to creators, run usability tests, track the impact of your work and proactively suggest iterations.

    First year: Help the team improve our activation, free-to-paid, trial conversion, and early retention rates, so that more creators upgrade, stay on Kit, and find real value. Turn our upsell, discount and proposal change moments into one coherent experience instead of a set of one-off prompts.

    Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration, enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.

    You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.

    Deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.

    It has been revealed that drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.

    Work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.

    Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.

    Sources indicate that feed the product. Custom integrations you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

    • Conduct QA on all email and SMS campaigns and journeys in Iterable prior to launch to ensure every element is configured correctly and functions as intended.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that winona is one of the leading telemedicine companies providing HRT for women in menopause. We’ve built all of our technology in-house including an EHR, patient care admin system, patient portal, website, marketing technology etc. Winona has two compounding pharmacies and a team of in-house physicians providing world-class care via a fully vertically integrated business model.

    We are seeking a detail-oriented QA Specialist to ensure that every email and SMS campaign and journey is configured correctly and functions as intended prior to launch. This role spans campaign configuration and tracking, content and design review, and cross-platform QA — identifying and resolving issues before they reach our audience.

    Seniority Level: Junior–Mid Level.

    Conduct QA on all email and SMS campaigns and journeys in Iterable prior to launch to ensure every element is configured correctly and functions as intended.

    Verify campaign and journey names against Winona’s naming conventions (name, year, event, medium and audience).

    Review journey configuration, including start tiles, suppressions, scheduled send dates and times, tile logic and conditionals, entry limits, exit rules and journey event tracking.

    Confirm that monthly and recurring journeys are refreshed with updated start tiles prior to each send.

    Verify that campaign labels are applied correctly (audience, segments, category, goal and month/year).

    Confirm that the appropriate conversion events are assigned for each campaign type: prospect, customer upsell, Shop, community and live event campaigns.

    Review delivery settings, including quiet hours, send time optimization, frequency caps and performance alerts.

    Verify that link tracking is configured correctly, including Google Analytics, UTM parameters and custom link parameters.

    Review sender details: message type, from name, from email and reply-to address.

    Review email templates against Winona’s brand and design standards, including fonts, sizing, padding, CTA button styling, link formatting and footers.

    Test all links, CTA buttons and image links, and confirm that images include alt text.

    Proofread copy for accuracy, consistency and formatting.

    Send and review test proofs in light and dark mode on iOS and Android, across both Gmail and Apple Mail.

    Coordinate SMS test sends with the appropriate team members prior to testing.

    Conduct QA on email touchpoints that connect to Shopify, such as Shop campaigns and checkout-related flows, to ensure a seamless end-to-end experience.

    Follow and help maintain internal templating documentation, QA checklists and the HTML template library.

    Communicate complications, errors and inconsistencies to the lifecycle team clearly and promptly, and track them through resolution.

    Recommend improvements to QA processes and standards on an ongoing basis.

    At least 3 years of experience performing QA within an ESP like Iterable or similar platforms.

    Working knowledge of HTML and CSS for email.

    Exceptional attention to detail and consistent checklist execution.

    Understanding of how emails render across clients, devices and dark mode.

    Clear written communication for reporting issues.

    Proficiency with Handlebars or dynamic content personalization.

    Shopify experience, particularly with checkout and order flows.

    Experience with email testing tools such as Litmus or Email on Acid.

    Familiarity with Google Analytics and UTM tracking.

    Experience with ClickUp or similar project management tools.

    Knowledge of SMS best practices and compliance standards (CAN-SPAM, CASL).

    As a full-time independent contractor, you’ll enjoy:.

    Remote-first, work wherever you choose.

    Paid non-working holidays per country of residence.

    SailPoint Intros Upcoming Capabilities to Address Agentic AI Identity Security Challenge

    📅 12 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that AI agents are moving from experiments into everyday enterprise environments, but the security controls around them are not keeping pace, according to enterprise identity security company SailPoint.
    • Industry observers note that that gap could become harder to ignore as organizations give agents more autonomy.
    • Sources indicate that sailPoint, which develops identity security and access governance technology for enterprises, is responding with a collection of upcoming identity security capabilities unveiled at its Navigate 2026 conference.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that AI agents are moving from experiments into everyday enterprise environments, but the security controls around them are not keeping pace, according to enterprise identity security company SailPoint. In its latest Horizons of Identity Security report, SailPoint found that 79% of enterprises already have AI agents running in production, while just 2% have deployed identity security tools specifically designed to govern them.

    Industry observers note that that gap could become harder to ignore as organizations give agents more autonomy. Agents can increasingly access applications, sensitive data, and credentials, and in some cases take actions on a user's behalf, effectively creating a new class of identity that IT and security teams need to manage.

    Sources indicate that sailPoint, which develops identity security and access governance technology for enterprises, is responding with a collection of upcoming identity security capabilities unveiled at its Navigate 2026 conference. The company is expanding its Agentic Fabric to discover "shadow AI" agents and provide runtime authorization and controls capable of immediately disabling an agent.

    The organization also introduced what it calls SailPoint Autonomous Agents, specialized AI agents designed to govern other agents. The security agents can monitor runtime activity, intercept threats, and adjust permissions while allowing legitimate agents to continue operating, SailPoint said.

    The idea reflects one of the challenges created by increasingly autonomous AI systems: Traditional human approval processes may not be fast enough to govern software capable of taking large numbers of actions on its own.

    "The idea that a security admin is going to review and approve access for a group of autonomous agents making 10,000 tool calls a second isn't just outdated — it's a fantasy," SailPoint CTO Chandra Gnanasambandam noted.

    Another part of SailPoint's approach focuses on visibility.

    Upcoming endpoint and browser sensors, along with SIEM and XDR telemetry and non-human identity discovery capabilities, are designed to uncover agents, MCP servers, credentials, tools, and data stores that haven't been brought under an organization's identity program.

    According to recent reports, the firm is also introducing Autonomous Identity Security Posture Management, or A-ISPM, which uses identity information from its Atlas platform to identify dormant accounts, orphaned access, shadow administrators, and other potentially risky access paths. Organizations can then revoke access, disable an identity or AI agent, assign an owner or automate enforcement.

    Just-in-Time provisioning is another part of the strategy. Rather than giving people, service accounts, and AI agents permanent access, permissions can be granted when needed and subjected to conditions such as reauthentication or a business justification.

    Sources indicate that capabilities across SailPoint's Agentic Fabric, Human Fabric, and Atlas platforms are beginning to roll out globally. A-ISPM and several other confirmed features are expected in the manufacturer's fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.

    "Autonomous agents are no longer just experimental copilots; they are becoming the primary execution layer of modern enterprises," SailPoint President Matt Mills said.

    For more information, go to the SailPoint site.

    #158169. Survey: Most Organizations Are Not Consistently Measuring AI Value Against Costs

    📅 19 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (597 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Survey: Most Organizations Are Not Consistently Measuring AI Value Against Costs

    📅 19 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.
    • Average planned AI investment for the next 12 months has risen to $210 million, compared with $186 million in the first quarter of 2026.
    • The findings are based on responses from 2,131 senior leaders across 20 countries and jurisdictions, surveyed between July 23 and August 26, 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, A new study from consulting firm KPMG found that while AI investment continues to grow, relatively few organizations consistently measure whether the technology's benefits justify its costs. The organization's Global AI Pulse Q3 2026 report found that 89% of organizations report measurable value from AI, while just 12% consistently assess that value against costs across the organization.

    Average planned AI investment for the next 12 months has risen to $210 million, compared with $186 million in the first quarter of 2026.

    The findings are based on responses from 2,131 senior leaders across 20 countries and jurisdictions, surveyed between July 23 and August 26, 2026.

    Most organizations have established ways to track AI spending: 61% review costs during project approval, and 59% monitor them once systems are operating.

    It has been revealed that consistently connecting those costs to value remains less common. Beyond the 12% that do so across the organization, another 26% assess value against costs for most initiatives.

    In a recent development, organizations reporting established AI returns have stronger measurement practices. Among this group, 48% consistently assess value against costs, four times the proportion in the overall survey group.

    Cost-monitoring dashboards are also more common among organizations reporting established returns: 77% use them, compared with 43% of those still experimenting.

    "The organizations seeing a return did the implementation and the transformation properly: guardrails in place, workforce ready, data cleaned up," said Priya Emmanuel, global head of aIQ at KPMG International. "That is a sequence, not a secret.".

    Organizations are also developing more formal systems to manage AI deployment.

    Fifty-five percent operate a formal AI management layer, which KPMG calls a "harness layer," comprising controls and tools between AI models and business applications.

    Industry observers note that security and identity controls, along with data access controls, were the most common capabilities, each reported by 43% of respondents. Model routing, which determines which model handles a particular task, was reported by 23%.

    Meanwhile, 53% assign accountability for AI-informed decisions to a named executive, the CEO, or an executive committee.

    The proportion reporting significant employee adoption of AI agents rose from 25% in the first quarter to 34% in the third quarter.

    Cybersecurity concerns were more common among organizations with mature AI programs.

    Half of those reporting established AI returns identified cybersecurity as a barrier, compared with roughly one-third of those still experimenting.

    Overall, 86% of respondents remarked their organizations are adapting their cybersecurity operating models to address AI-accelerated threats.

    The report identifies accountability, operational resilience, and cost management as priorities as AI becomes more embedded in business operations.

    Sources indicate that "Many organizations have made AI models widely available and track their use," said Swaminathan Chandrasekaran, head of the US AI Center of Excellence at KPMG. "But consumption alone is not a strategy.".

    For the full report, visit the KPMG site.

    #158148. Tech Report: Report: Cyber Attacks Increasingly Exploit Trusted Workplace Tools

    📅 21 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (688 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Thejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Report: Cyber Attacks Increasingly Exploit Trusted Workplace Tools

    📅 21 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (688 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that in its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick users into giving them access to enterprise networks.
    • Ontinue's report says the trouble is that these attacks blend in with ordinary workday communication, which makes them harder to catch.
    • "The majority of effective attacks today don't rely on sophisticated exploits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that in its latest threat intelligence report, Ontinue found that attackers are increasingly using trusted workplace tools to trick users into giving them access to enterprise networks. Approximately 30% of organizations monitored by the cybersecurity tech giant experienced at least one attempt to impersonate IT support through Microsoft Teams during the first half of 2026. About one in every 990 external Teams contacts showed signs of someone pretending to be an internal IT worker.

    Ontinue's report says the trouble is that these attacks blend in with ordinary workday communication, which makes them harder to catch.

    "The majority of effective attacks today don't rely on sophisticated exploits. They rely on trust," Balazs Greksza, director of Advanced Threat Operations at Ontinue, said in the company's announcement.

    Ontinue broke down how a typical attack works: An employee gets an unexpected Teams message or call from someone claiming to work in the organization's IT department. The person warns of a security problem, a software problem or an update that can't wait. Then they walk the employee through opening Windows Quick Assist, installing remote-access software, or running a PowerShell command. Following those steps can hand the attacker control of the employee's computer, often without the employee realizing it.

    Recent findings suggest that the approach is very similar to the Black Basta ransomware group, which helped popularize similar attacks in 2024. Unfortunately, Ontinue found the technique has since been adopted by other cybercriminal groups, including some with no known link to Black Basta.

    Some threat agents are also combining tactics. They might first overwhelm an employee's inbox with unwanted e-mails, then reach out through Teams pretending to be IT support offering to fix the problem.

    "Phishing no longer resides solely in your inbox. It has spread across the entire corporate communications environment," mentioned Mika Aalto, co-founder and CEO of Hoxhunt.

    Sources indicate that teams impersonation is only part of the problem. Ontinue also found attackers taking advantage of legitimate Microsoft sign-in processes. Between May and June, researchers identified 10 confirmed device-code phishing compromises across five customer tenants.

    In these attacks, criminals trick employees into completing what appears to be a normal Microsoft authentication process. But doing so can give the attacker access to the employee's account and system without actually breaking their password.

    The report also found attackers using blockchain-based infrastructure to hide malicious activity, accounting for more than 25% of confirmed malicious ClickFix findings.

    It has been revealed that "Attackers are no longer looking for gaps in your perimeter. They are looking for the systems your organization already trusts and finding ways to move through them undetected," said Shane Barney, chief information security officer at Keeper Security.

    Sources indicate that the security firm notes that IT needs to keep a closer eye on unexpected Teams contacts, remote-support requests, suspicious PowerShell activity, and changes to authentication settings. Employees should also confirm sensitive requests through established internal channels, rather than relying on the name or account that appears on their screen.

    Aviv Nahum, co-founder and CEO of Above Security, noted that AI is making these attacks more convincing by helping criminals imitate familiar voices, writing styles, and conversations.

    "The security model therefore must shift from 'does this look real?' to 'can I independently verify that this person is who they claim to be?'" Nahum mentioned.

    The full Ontinue report can be found here.

    Chris Paoli (@ChrisPaoli5) is the associate editor for Converge360.

    Storage Platform Engineer at Supabase

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realworkfromanywhere

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that supabase runs millions of Postgres databases, and storage performance is now one of the biggest levers on how fast, reliable, and affordable they are.
    • As the senior engineer driving storage, you'll own this effort end to end: the architecture and build-vs-buy decisions, integration into our compute platform, and operating the system in production.
    • It has been revealed that your first goal is raw Postgres I/O performance at scale.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that supabase runs millions of Postgres databases, and storage performance is now one of the biggest levers on how fast, reliable, and affordable they are. We're building a software-defined, NVMe-over-Fabrics storage platform underneath Supabase Postgres. Postgres stays unmodified, and the newly introduced layer delivers near-local-NVMe performance with the durability and flexibility of networked storage.

    As the senior engineer driving storage, you'll own this effort end to end: the architecture and build-vs-buy decisions, integration into our compute platform, and operating the system in production.

    It has been revealed that your first goal is raw Postgres I/O performance at scale. In the longer term, the layer you build will provide the block-level snapshots and copy-on-write clones behind database branching, fast restores, and instant resizes. Because it's software-defined, it will also travel with us as we expand beyond a single cloud provider into multi-cloud and colocated infrastructure.

    This is a foundational, high-ownership role. You'll set the technical direction for storage at Supabase and help grow the team around it.

    Lead the architecture of Supabase's NVMe-oF storage platform, including evaluating and deciding between adopting existing software-defined storage and building on SPDK.

    Integrate networked block storage into our Kubernetes-based compute platform through CSI drivers and custom controllers, covering provisioning, attach/detach, resizing, and migration.

    Make Postgres fast on networked storage by profiling and tuning the full I/O path, from fsync, WAL, and checkpoints through the kernel block layer, NVMe/TCP, and the network.

    Design for durability and availability, including replication or erasure coding, failure domains, failover, and data-integrity verification.

    Build I/O isolation and QoS so that noisy neighbors can't degrade other tenants.

    Set performance and reliability SLOs, and build the benchmarking and observability to hold the system to them.

    Design the layer for block-level snapshots and copy-on-write clones, laying the groundwork for database branching.

    Keep the platform portable across AWS, other clouds, and bare-metal/colo.

    Have experience with Kubernetes controllers and/or CSI drivers.

    Have been on call for large production systems.

    Communicate clearly in writing and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

    Experience with AWS networking and instance storage at scale (ENA, placement, bandwidth limits).

    • Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers.
    • We’re looking for a Software Engineer, Postgres Tooling to join our CLI team and help build the open-source tools developers use to change their Postgres schemas safely.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    We’re looking for a Software Engineer, Postgres Tooling to join our CLI team and help build the open-source tools developers use to change their Postgres schemas safely. You’ll join as a co-maintainer of pg-delta, our schema diff and migration engine, and grow into leading it.

    Given two databases, or a database and a folder of SQL files describing the schema you want, pg-delta works out the differences and generates the migration to get from one to the other. It powers supabase db diff, db pull, and declarative schemas, and it runs underneath Supabase’s platform, branching, and AI agent workflows. Every migration it generates is verified on a throwaway clone before it’s trusted, and it’s tested against 331 scenarios on PostgreSQL 14–18. We’re now working toward a stable, standalone 1.0 release for any Postgres developer, on Supabase or not.

    This is a correctness-first role. The SQL this tool generates runs against production databases, so privilege safety and avoiding data loss are non-negotiable. It’s a great fit for someone who loves Postgres at the catalog level, enjoys compiler-style problems, and thrives in async, fast-paced environments.

    Co-maintain pg-delta: review and merge changes, including PRs written by AI agents, and grow into its lead maintainer.

    Own correctness: triage bug reports from GitHub and support, fix diff and dependency-ordering bugs, and extend test coverage across Postgres versions.

    Make sure generated migrations are privilege-safe and never silently lose data, by detecting destructive changes and rewriting them into safe equivalents where possible.

    Help take pg-delta to a stable 1.0: a public API with a semver contract, documentation, and broader coverage of Postgres extensions.

    Work with the open-source community: triage problems, review outside contributions, and say no gracefully when a request doesn’t fit.

    Work with the teams across Supabase that build on pg-delta, so migrations are generated and run the same way everywhere.

    Write the design docs and technical strategy that set the tool’s direction, working async across teams.

    Sources indicate that share the CLI team’s on-call rotation. Weekdays are covered follow-the-sun, and because we ship packaged software that users can roll back, pages are rare.

    Have 8+ years of experience as a software engineer, including deep, hands-on work with PostgreSQL.

    Know Postgres internals at the catalog level: pg_catalog, pg_depend, object ownership, grants and default privileges, RLS policies, and extension membership.

    Understand DDL and migration semantics: which changes take locks, which can’t run inside a transaction, how dependencies determine ordering, and how to spot a destructive change.

    Treat a migration that silently loosens access as a top-severity bug.

    Write strong TypeScript, and design tests for correctness, such as differential, property-based, or corpus testing across multiple Postgres versions.

    Are comfortable with compiler-style problems: dependency graphs, topological ordering, cycle handling, and diffing.

    Can confidently review complex changes in an intricate codebase, including AI-generated PRs.

    Have owned software in production with users in the loop: staged rollouts, error monitoring, and triaging real bug reports.

    Have led a technical project across several teams, from an ambiguous start to production.

    Communicate clearly in writing and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

    Nice to have, roughly in order of how much they’d help:.

    Have built or maintained schema diff or migration tooling (such as migra, pg-schema-diff, Atlas, pgroll, sqitch, Prisma Migrate, or Flyway/Liquibase), or worked with pg_dump internals.

    Open-source maintainer experience: API contracts, semver, documentation, and community triage.

    Familiarity with Postgres extensions such as pg_cron, pgmq, pg_partman, vault, pg_net, pgvector, or PostGIS.

    Contributions to Postgres itself, or authorship of a Postgres extension.

    Experience with Supabase or another managed Postgres platform.
